name: N-Queens (Backtracking)
description: The N-Queens problem places N chess queens on an N×N chessboard so that no two queens threaten each other. This classic backtracking problem demonstrates constraint satisfaction - queens cannot share the same row, column, or diagonal. The algorithm tries placing queens one by one, backtracking when a placement violates constraints, exploring all possible valid configurations.

aiExplanation.content: The N-Queens problem is a classic example of backtracking - a systematic way to explore all possible solutions by trying options and undoing (backtracking) when constraints are violated. The algorithm places queens row by row, checking if each placement is safe (no conflicts with previously placed queens). When it reaches a dead end, it backtracks to try different positions. This exhaustive search with pruning is essential for constraint satisfaction problems, puzzle solving, and combinatorial optimization.
